citations.text: The rule is triggered when a borrower fails to pay by the due date under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement. Firms need a way to identify missed payments at the point they occur so that the timing obligation can be met. Whether existing arrangements can do this is unknown.

aiEvidenceClaims: 1. The rule is triggered when a borrower fails to pay by the due date under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement. Firms need a way to identify missed payments at the point they occur so that the timing obligation can be met. Whether existing arrangements can do this is unknown. [sections: REG-1]

2. The firm must act 'as soon as possible' after a missed payment. The rule sets no fixed number of days, so the firm will need to define and justify an internal timing standard. Expert confirmation of the FCA's timing expectation is needed. [sections: REG-1]

3. Standalone obligation to notify the borrower both that the missed payment has occurred and about any sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance. This implies that notification content must draw on accurate arrears and charges data. The firm's data availability is not known. [sections: REG-1]

4. Standalone obligation to provide sufficient information for the borrower to understand which agreement the missed payment relates to, adverse consequences, likely adverse consequences and, where relevant, mitigation steps. This is an outcome standard rather than a fixed content list, so the firm will need to decide and evidence what is 'sufficient'. It also requires judgement on what counts as adverse and when a mitigation step is relevant; both need expert input. [sections: REG-1]

5. The firm must assess adverse consequences that it considers likely to arise from the missed payment. This points to a need for a documented judgement process and evidence of how likely consequences were determined. The expected standard of evidence is uncertain. [sections: REG-1]

6. The information required under paragraph (2) must be provided together, so the notification and the supporting information cannot be split across separate communications. Communication templates and delivery processes may need to be designed to issue them as a single communication. Current practice is unknown. [sections: REG-1]

7. 'Payment' refers to repayment of capital and excludes charges for non-compliance. A missed charge alone does not trigger the rule, although unpaid charges must still be notified once a capital payment is missed. Firms will need to apply this scope distinction in their trigger logic. [sections: REG-1]

rawProviderOutput.summary: Draft impact suggestion for CONC 7.20.1R (effective 2026-07-15 per instrument commencement). The rule requires a firm, as soon as possible after a missed payment under a regulated deferred payment credit agreement, to (a) notify the borrower of the missed payment and of unpaid sums, and (b) provide sufficient information for the borrower to understand the relevant agreement, adverse consequences, likely adverse consequences and relevant mitigation steps, with all of this information provided together. No organisational systems, controls or incident data were supplied, so firm-specific impact cannot be determined and no firm facts are assumed. This is a draft for human review and is not regulatory advice.

limbs.text: This rule applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (‘a missed payment’).
As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must:
notify the borrower:
that the missed payment has occurred; and
about any sums which have become payable under the regulated deferred payment credit agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement); and
provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand:
which regulated deferred payment credit agreement the missed payment relates to;
any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment;
any adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment; and
(where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences.
The information required under (2) must be provided together.
In this rule references to ‘payment’ refer to the repayment of capital but exclude payment of a charge for non-compliance with a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.

fullTestPlan.frequency: Recommended initial test before the 15 July 2026 effective date, once the notification process is confirmed. Thereafter, risk-based periodic testing, for example quarterly in the first year, with ad hoc retesting after template, system or policy changes. The frequency requires human confirmation.
fullTestPlan.objective: To recommend procedures and evidence for assessing whether the firm, as soon as possible after a missed payment, detects the missed payment (CONC 7.20.1R(1)), notifies the borrower (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)), provides sufficient information (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)) and provides that information together (CONC 7.20.1R(3)). The existing detective control (CTRL-1) is NOT_TESTED and is assumed to cover detection only. The plan therefore tests the regulatory outcome end to end and identifies any notification control that must be mapped. This is a draft for human review. It records no test result and accepts no exception.
procedure: 1. Confirm scope and design (CTRL-1): a human reviewer should obtain the control's design documentation and confirm whether it covers regulated deferred payment credit agreements. They should also confirm whether it applies the CONC 7.20.1R(4) definition of payment (capital repayment only, excluding charges for non-compliance). If the control does not notify borrowers, identify and document the separate control or process that does. Do not assume one exists.

2. Population completeness: reconcile a period's contractual due-date schedules and payment receipts for in-scope agreements against the control's missed-payment exception output. Test for missed payments not detected, for non-capital charges wrongly treated as missed payments, and for in-scope agreements missing from the feed.
3. Detection timing: for a risk-based sample of detected missed payments, compare the due date and time with the detection timestamp to assess detection lag.

4. Notification delivery (2)(a): for the same sample, trace each case to evidence that the borrower was notified. Check that the notice states that the missed payment occurred (2)(a)(i) and states the sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance (2)(a)(ii). Recompute the sums from the ledger and compare them with the notice.

5. Information sufficiency (2)(b): assess each notice or communication against the content elements: the identity of the agreement (2)(b)(i); the existing adverse consequences (2)(b)(ii); the adverse consequences the firm considers likely (2)(b)(iii); and, where relevant, mitigation steps (2)(b)(iv). Ask an independent reviewer to judge whether a borrower could understand the position, using documented criteria that have been agreed with compliance.

6. Judgement evidence: review the records, templates or decision rules showing how the firm decided which consequences are likely and which mitigation steps are relevant, and test their consistent application across cases, including borrowers with different circumstances.

7. Together requirement (3): verify that the information required under (2) was provided together in a single communication or delivery. Flag cases where the elements were split across channels or times.

8. Timeliness: measure the elapsed time from the missed payment to delivery of the notification and information. Compare it with the firm's documented 'as soon as possible' standard. This standard needs expert or FCA-aligned confirmation, because the rule fixes no number of days.

9. Exceptions and escalation: for cases where the notification was missing, late, incomplete or split, document the cause and refer the case to the control owner and compliance for human decision. Do not close or accept exceptions within this plan.
fullTestPlan.reviewType: Design and operating effectiveness review (draft proposal) covering detection and the delivery of borrower notification and information outcomes
evidenceRequirements: Control design documents and system configuration for CTRL-1, including the scope of agreements and the payment definition applied
Agreement schedules, payment ledgers and the missed-payment exception reports for the period

procedure: 1. Confirm scope and design (CTRL-1): a human reviewer should obtain the control's design documentation and confirm whether it covers regulated deferred payment credit agreements. They should also confirm whether it applies the CONC 7.20.1R(4) definition of payment (capital repayment only, excluding charges for non-compliance). If the control does not notify borrowers, identify and document the separate control or process that does. Do not assume one exists.

2. Population completeness: reconcile a period's contractual due-date schedules and payment receipts for in-scope agreements against the control's missed-payment exception output. Test for missed payments not detected, for non-capital charges wrongly treated as missed payments, and for in-scope agreements missing from the feed.
3. Detection timing: for a risk-based sample of detected missed payments, compare the due date and time with the detection timestamp to assess detection lag.

4. Notification delivery (2)(a): for the same sample, trace each case to evidence that the borrower was notified. Check that the notice states that the missed payment occurred (2)(a)(i) and states the sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance (2)(a)(ii). Recompute the sums from the ledger and compare them with the notice.

5. Information sufficiency (2)(b): assess each notice or communication against the content elements: the identity of the agreement (2)(b)(i); the existing adverse consequences (2)(b)(ii); the adverse consequences the firm considers likely (2)(b)(iii); and, where relevant, mitigation steps (2)(b)(iv). Ask an independent reviewer to judge whether a borrower could understand the position, using documented criteria that have been agreed with compliance.

6. Judgement evidence: review the records, templates or decision rules showing how the firm decided which consequences are likely and which mitigation steps are relevant, and test their consistent application across cases, including borrowers with different circumstances.

7. Together requirement (3): verify that the information required under (2) was provided together in a single communication or delivery. Flag cases where the elements were split across channels or times.

8. Timeliness: measure the elapsed time from the missed payment to delivery of the notification and information. Compare it with the firm's documented 'as soon as possible' standard. This standard needs expert or FCA-aligned confirmation, because the rule fixes no number of days.

9. Exceptions and escalation: for cases where the notification was missing, late, incomplete or split, document the cause and refer the case to the control owner and compliance for human decision. Do not close or accept exceptions within this plan.

limbs.text: This rule applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (‘a missed payment’).
As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must:
notify the borrower:
that the missed payment has occurred; and
about any sums which have become payable under the regulated deferred payment credit agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement); and
provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand:
which regulated deferred payment credit agreement the missed payment relates to;
any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment;
any adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment; and
(where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences.
The information required under (2) must be provided together.
In this rule references to ‘payment’ refer to the repayment of capital but exclude payment of a charge for non-compliance with a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.

risks.title: Failure to notify borrower promptly of a missed payment and unpaid sums under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)

risk.title: Failure to notify borrower promptly of a missed payment and unpaid sums under CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a)
risk.description:
The firm may not notify the borrower, as soon as possible after a missed payment, that the payment has occurred and of any sums that have become payable but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance). Risk drivers include missed payment detection, timing of notification, and the accuracy of unpaid sums data. Because the rule fixes no number of days, the timing standard needs expert confirmation. This proposal overlaps with an existing approved catalogue risk, which is mapped below.

Inherent rating: HIGH (provisional) — CONC 7.20.1R(2)(a) is a binding rule requiring the firm to notify the borrower as soon as possible after a missed payment of the missed payment and of any unpaid sums, including unpaid charges. If this is missed, borrowers may not know they are in arrears, may incur further charges or adverse credit consequences, and the firm may breach a binding FCA rule that takes effect on 15 July 2026. The rating is drawn from the verified quotation in REG-1 and the impact summary in IMP-1; it is an inherent rating only and requires human validation.
Residual rating: UNASSESSED — no control-effectiveness evidence is available.

If the control does not notify borrowers, identify and document the separate control or process that does. Do not assume one exists.

2. Population completeness: reconcile a period's contractual due-date schedules and payment receipts for in-scope agreements against the control's missed-payment exception output. Test for missed payments not detected, for non-capital charges wrongly treated as missed payments, and for in-scope agreements missing from the feed.
3. Detection timing: for a risk-based sample of detected missed payments, compare the due date and time with the detection timestamp to assess detection lag.

4. Notification delivery (2)(a): for the same sample, trace each case to evidence that the borrower was notified. Check that the notice states that the missed payment occurred (2)(a)(i) and states the sums payable but unpaid, including unpaid charges for non-compliance (2)(a)(ii). Recompute the sums from the ledger and compare them with the notice.

5. Information sufficiency (2)(b): assess each notice or communication against the content elements: the identity of the agreement (2)(b)(i); the existing adverse consequences (2)(b)(ii); the adverse consequences the firm considers likely (2)(b)(iii); and, where relevant, mitigation steps (2)(b)(iv). Ask an independent reviewer to judge whether a borrower could understand the position, using documented criteria that have been agreed with compliance.

6. Judgement evidence: review the records, templates or decision rules showing how the firm decided which consequences are likely and which mitigation steps are relevant, and test their consistent application across cases, including borrowers with different circumstances.

7. Together requirement (3): verify that the information required under (2) was provided together in a single communication or delivery. Flag cases where the elements were split across channels or times.

8. Timeliness: measure the elapsed time from the missed payment to delivery of the notification and information. Compare it with the firm's documented 'as soon as possible' standard. This standard needs expert or FCA-aligned confirmation, because the rule fixes no number of days.

9. Exceptions and escalation: for cases where the notification was missing, late, incomplete or split, document the cause and refer the case to the control owner and compliance for human decision. Do not close or accept exceptions within this plan.
testPlan.reviewType: Design and operating effectiveness review (draft proposal) covering detection and the delivery of borrower notification and information outcomes
evidenceRequirements: Control design documents and system configuration for CTRL-1, including the scope of agreements and the payment definition applied
Agreement schedules, payment ledgers and the missed-payment exception reports for the period
Detection and notification timestamps and system logs
Copies of the notices sent, with templates and version history, and channel and delivery records
Ledger extracts supporting the sums stated as unpaid
Documented criteria for adverse and likely consequences, for relevant mitigation steps and for the 'as soon as possible' standard, with approvals
Reviewer working papers recording the sample selection rationale and the independent sufficiency assessments
Exception log with root-cause notes and owner referrals

limbs.text: This rule applies where a borrower has failed to make a payment by the time it has fallen due under the terms of a regulated deferred payment credit agreement (‘a missed payment’).
As soon as possible after a missed payment has occurred the firm must:
notify the borrower:
that the missed payment has occurred; and
about any sums which have become payable under the regulated deferred payment credit agreement but remain unpaid (including unpaid charges for non-compliance with the agreement); and
provide the borrower with sufficient information for the borrower to understand:
which regulated deferred payment credit agreement the missed payment relates to;
any adverse consequences for the borrower arising out of the missed payment;
any adverse consequences for the borrower that the firm considers are likely to arise out of the missed payment; and
(where relevant) any steps the borrower can take to mitigate those adverse consequences.
The information required under (2) must be provided together.
In this rule references to ‘payment’ refer to the repayment of capital but exclude payment of a charge for non-compliance with a regulated deferred payment credit agreement.

uncertainties: Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)): What period satisfies "as soon as possible"? The rule fixes no number of days; the FCA expectation on timing needs expert confirmation.
Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)): What level of detail is "sufficient information for the borrower to understand"? This is an outcome standard, not a content list.
Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(ii)): Which consequences count as adverse (charges, credit reporting, enforcement, loss of facility)? The rule does not enumerate them.
Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(iii)): The firm is asked to judge likely consequences. What evidence of that judgement is expected?
Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(iii)): Which consequences count as adverse (charges, credit reporting, enforcement, loss of facility)? The rule does not enumerate them.
Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(iv)): When is a mitigation step "relevant"? The firm must decide per case; expert view on defensible criteria is needed.
Expert judgement needed (CONC 7.20.1R(2)(b)(iv)): Which consequences count as adverse (charges, credit reporting, enforcement, loss of facility)? The rule does not enumerate them.
